findings.problem: SampleWorkflow has no state machine — any combination of is_validated/is_sent/sent_at_epoch_ms is allowed, including is_sent=true with is_validated=false, or duplicate transitions with no history
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct and mutate SampleWorkflow into logically impossible states (e.g., sent but not validated), violating domain invariants at compile time
findings.fix: Replace fields with a single State enum (e.g., State { Unvalidated, Validated, Sent { sent_at: u64 } }) and make transition methods fallible on State

findings.problem: status is a pub String, allowing any arbitrary value ("sent", "sent ", "SENT", "", "deleted") — no finite set of valid domain states is enforced by the type
findings.failure_mode: Pattern matches on status strings are brittle and incomplete; callers can set status to an unhandled value and the program silently accepts it instead of failing at the boundary
findings.fix: Replace String with a sealed Status enum and match exhaustively; remove pub accessors that expose raw status strings

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent booleans with no enforced ordering — nothing prevents both being true, both false after a reset, or is_sent=true before is_validated
findings.failure_mode: Logic branches on is_sent will execute for objects that were never validated; concurrent or retry paths can produce inconsistent lifecycle snapshots
findings.fix: Fold lifecycle booleans into a single State enum with explicit transition variants (Unvalidated -> Validated -> Sent) and make transitions single-dispatch fallible methods

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is decoupled from is_sent — is_sent can be true while sent_at_epoch_ms is None (contradictory), or sent_at_epoch_ms can be Some while is_sent is false
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code that checks is_sent before reading sent_at_epoch_ms.unwraps will panic; code that reads sent_at_epoch_ms without checking is_sent will process unsent items
findings.fix: Move the timestamp into the Sent variant of a State enum (e.g., State::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }) so Some/None is guaranteed by the variant, not an independent Option

findings.problem: id is a plain String with no newtype — callers can pass empty strings, non-ASCII strings, or mix up IDs from different domains without compile-time distinction
findings.failure_mode: Calling send_with_id("") or send_with_id(other_workflow.id.clone()) compiles and may corrupt workflow state; IDs cannot be validated at parse time
findings.fix: Introduce a pub struct WorkflowId(String) with a smart constructor fn new_workflow_id(s: &str) -> Result<WorkflowId, WorkflowError> that validates non-empty and rejects illegal characters

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts raw SampleWorkflow with no validation — raw primitives and booleans cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly and mark_sent will happily mutate them into a sent state
findings.failure_mode: A caller passing is_sent=false, is_validated=false, status="" will have mark_sent set status="sent" and is_sent=true, creating a sent record with no validation history and no audit trail
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with fn transition_to_sent(state: State) -> Result<State, TransitionError> or use a builder/constructor that validates preconditions (is_validated) before returning a Sent variant

findings.problem: mark_sent unconditionally sets status="sent" and is_sent=true without checking any preconditions (e.g., is_validated must be true, status must not already be "sent")
findings.failure_mode: Duplicate send calls succeed silently; unvalidated items can be marked sent; re-sending overwrites sent_at_epoch_ms with None, losing audit data
findings.fix: Guard with a precondition check: if item.status == "sent" return Err(WorkflowError::AlreadySent); require is_validated==true before allowing the transition

findings.problem: mark_sent uses "sent".to_string() which allocates a heap String on every call — the pure domain transition should use an enum variant, not heap-allocate a literal string
findings.failure_mode: Every transition allocates unnecessarily; in hot paths this becomes a measurable allocation overhead; the String allocation hides the fact that the transition is a simple state change
findings.fix: Replace with an enum variant (State::Sent) which is zero-cost — no heap allocation, no String indirection

findings.problem: All fields (id, status, is_validated, is_sent, sent_at_epoch_ms) are pub and mutable — any caller can mutate any field without going through a domain method
findings.failure_mode: External code can set item.is_sent = false after mark_sent, reverting the sent state without any audit trail or invariant check
findings.fix: Make fields private and expose only domain-method accessors; implement DDD aggregate pattern with controlled mutation

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for mark_sent or any performance-sensitive path. The .to_string() allocation on every transition is unmeasured.
findings.failure_mode: If mark_sent is in a hot loop, the per-call allocation may become a bottleneck; without a baseline there is no way to detect regression
findings.fix: Add a Criterion or simple microbenchmark for mark_sent comparing current String-based approach against an enum-based approach

findings.problem: No profiler evidence (flamegraph, perf record, or similar) exists to verify the allocation pattern or identify actual bottlenecks in this module
findings.failure_mode: Optimizations may target the wrong code path; the real bottleneck could be elsewhere (parsing, I/O, serialization)
findings.fix: Run cargo flamegraph or perf record on a representative workload and include the profile in the evidence bundle

findings.problem: No allocation profiling (valgrind/dhat/memfd) evidence exists to quantify the number and size of heap allocations per mark_sent call
findings.failure_mode: Unbounded allocation count could cause memory pressure in long-running services
findings.fix: Use dhat or valgrind --tool=massif to measure allocations per transition and compare against enum-based implementation

findings.problem: No second-ring evidence (property tests, fuzzing, or state-machine property tests) exists to verify that all state transitions maintain invariants across arbitrary sequences of operations
findings.failure_mode: Edge-case state transition sequences that violate invariants may not be caught by unit tests alone
findings.fix: Add proptest-based property tests that generate random state transition sequences and assert invariant preservation (e.g., sent implies validated, sent_at_epoch_ms is present when sent)

findings.problem: No evidence that required verification commands (cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, cargo test) were actually run for this review task
findings.failure_mode: Code may have formatting violations, clippy warnings, or compilation errors that go undetected
findings.fix: Run and report results for: cargo fmt --check, cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features, cargo clippy with strict lint flags, cargo test --workspace --all-features

All blockers are fixable by refactoring SampleWorkflow into a State enum with a smart constructor and fallible transition methods.
